tests.title: Unit 3: Digital Payment Mechanism – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: Asha receives a call from a person who says he is from her bank and asks for her UPI PIN so that a Rs 2,000 refund can be credited. The correct response is to:
options: Share only the first two digits so that the caller can verify the account
Approve the collect request that arrives while the caller is on the line
Share the PIN, because the bank needs it to credit the refund to her account
Refuse, because a PIN is required only to send money and never to receive it

questions.question_text: Ravi enters the UPI PIN to approve a "collect request" from an unknown number titled "Refund". The likely result is that:
options: Nothing happens, as collect requests are blocked by the NPCI
Money is debited from his account instead of being credited
His PIN is reset and the account is frozen for twenty-four hours
Money is credited to his account after the verification by the bank
questions.explanation: A collect request is a payment demand.

questions.question_text: A UPI payment between two accounts at different banks is possible mainly because UPI is:
options: Based on cheques which are cleared once a day by the clearing house
Interoperable, so that one app can link accounts of many banks
Restricted to the customers of the banks which belong to a single group
Owned by the largest bank, which lets other banks use its network

questions.question_text: Which entity owns and operates the UPI platform?
options: Reserve Bank of India, as the operator of UPI
Indian Banks' Association, as the owner of UPI
National Payments Corporation of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India, as the owner of UPI

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper with a basic phone wants to accept UPI payments without internet. The best option is:
options: The USSD-based *99# service of the NPCI
A net banking portal that works through a browser only
A credit card terminal that needs a card to be swiped
A mobile wallet that needs the internet connection

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of UPI 123PAY over a normal UPI app?
options: It works only for payments of electricity bills
It gives a cash discount on every transaction
It can be used on feature phones without a smartphone or internet
It allows payments of unlimited value without any PIN

questions.question_text: A person with a UPI Lite balance of Rs 500 pays Rs 100 at a tea stall. Compared with a regular UPI payment, the payment:
options: Requires a PIN and one-time password for every small payment
Does not require a PIN for the small value and is processed on-device
Is processed only on working days of the bank
Is processed only by the debit card used for the wallet

questions.question_text: A wallet issued by a company is regulated by the RBI as a:
options: Insurance product under the IRDAI regulations
Fixed deposit scheme under the Banking Regulation Act
Prepaid Payment Instrument under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act
Mutual fund scheme under the SEBI regulations

questions.question_text: A customer with a minimum-KYC wallet is limited mainly in that he can:
options: Withdraw unlimited cash from the ATMs without charges
Use the balance only for buying goods and services within a monthly limit
Transfer unlimited money abroad without any documents
Earn interest on the balance like a savings account

questions.question_text: The BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System) is useful because it:
options: Replaces the bank account of the user with a bill account
Allows the user to pay only the income tax and the GST
Lets a user pay electricity, gas, water and other bills on one platform
Allows the user to pay only the school fees and the exam fees

questions.question_text: AePS enables a person with a bank account linked to Aadhaar to:
options: Transfer money abroad by using the passport details
Take a loan from the bank by sending an e-mail
Pay for the goods with a credit card at a shopping mall
Withdraw cash using the fingerprint at a micro-ATM of a banking correspondent

questions.question_text: Salary payments to 500 employees credited together through the bank by an employer on the same day are most likely to use:
options: RTGS, one at a time for each of the employees
Cash withdrawn from the ATM
NACH credits
Demand drafts issued to each of the employees

questions.question_text: A car owner passes through a toll plaza without stopping, as the toll is automatically deducted. The system used is:
options: NEFT, based on the batch processing
FASTag, based on RFID technology
AePS, based on the biometric details
BHIM, based on the QR codes

questions.question_text: RuPay differs from Visa and Mastercard in that RuPay is:
options: A domestic card payment network launched by the NPCI
A foreign network which operates only outside India
A cheque clearing system for the government banks
A mobile wallet which does not use cards

questions.question_text: An online shop uses a service which securely sends the customer's card details to the bank for approval. This service is a:
options: Point of sale terminal in a shop
Clearing house of a bank
Payment gateway
Credit bureau for the customers

questions.question_text: A merchant at a restaurant uses a machine into which the customer's debit card is inserted and the PIN is typed. The machine is a:
options: Cash deposit machine of the bank
Passbook printing kiosk of the bank
Micro-ATM of the banking correspondent
POS terminal

questions.question_text: A card with an NFC chip allows the holder to:
options: Tap the card near the terminal to pay small amounts without a PIN
Receive foreign currency at the airport
Withdraw cash from any bank without the card
Skip the KYC for the opening of the bank account

questions.question_text: Tokenisation of a card means that:
options: The card details are shared with the merchant for faster payments
The CVV is printed on the receipt of every payment
The card is cancelled and a new card is issued to the customer
The actual card number is replaced by a unique token for the online payments

questions.question_text: A customer gets a message "your account will be blocked, click the link to update KYC". This is an example of:
options: Spoofing of the SIM card done by the telecom operator
Skimming, a fraud carried out at the ATM
Smishing, a fraud carried out through SMS
Vishing, a fraud carried out through voice calls

questions.question_text: A fraudster calls pretending to be a bank officer to obtain the card details. This is:
options: Vishing, a phishing attempt through voice calls
Spamming, a phishing attempt through bulk e-mails
Smishing, a phishing attempt through text messages
Pharming, a phishing attempt through fake websites

questions.question_text: A hidden device fitted to an ATM slot that copies the data of the card is used for:
options: Card skimming
Ransomware attack
Phishing of e-mail
Man in the middle attack

questions.question_text: A caller asks a customer to install a "screen sharing" app to fix a failed payment. The main danger is that:
options: The app will slow down the phone for a few days
The app will delete the contacts stored in the phone
The app will use too much of the battery of the phone
The caller can see the screen and the OTPs and operate the banking apps

questions.question_text: A UPI payment fails but the amount is debited from the account of the payer. The amount should normally be:
options: Kept by the bank as a charge for the failed payment
Returned only on a court order obtained by the customer
Returned only after one year to the customer
Reversed automatically within the timeline prescribed by the RBI

questions.question_text: If an unauthorised transaction occurs due to a bank's deficiency, and the customer reports it within three working days, the customer's liability is:
options: Equal to half of the amount of the transaction
Zero
Limited to Rs 10,000 for every transaction
Equal to the full amount of the transaction

questions.question_text: The national helpline number for reporting cyber financial fraud is:

tests.title: Unit 3: Digital Payment Mechanism – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: The online portal for filing a complaint on cybercrime in India is:
options: npci.org.in
rbi.org.in
cybercrime.gov.in
sebi.gov.in

questions.question_text: Which practice is MOST likely to expose a person to fraud?
options: Doing net banking over a free public Wi-Fi at a railway station
Updating the mobile banking app from the official store
Using a different password for each of the financial accounts
Enabling the alerts of transactions on the registered mobile

questions.question_text: Receiving an SMS for every debit and credit in the account is useful mainly because it:
options: Increases the balance of the account of the customer
Reduces the transaction charges of the account
Lets the bank advertise its other products
Allows the customer to detect the unauthorised transactions quickly

questions.question_text: The RBI-mandated additional factor of authentication for recurring card payments applies to a transaction if the amount is:
options: Below Rs 100 on every occasion
Paid in cash at the time of delivery
Paid through a cheque
Above the limit set by the RBI for e-mandates, at the time of the framing

questions.question_text: The e-rupee is best described as:
options: A prepaid card of a bank
A wallet of a mobile company
A cryptocurrency issued by a private company
A digital form of the legal tender issued by the RBI

questions.question_text: Private cryptocurrencies in India are:
options: Not recognised as legal tender
Accepted for payment of taxes
Legal tender issued by the RBI
Guaranteed by the government

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of digital payments?
options: Complete elimination of the risk of cyber fraud
A digital record of every transaction
Reduced dependence on cash
Convenience and speed of settlement

questions.question_text: The "digital divide" refers to:
options: The gap in the exchange rates of two currencies
The gap between those who can use technology and those who cannot
The gap in the budget of two governments
The gap in the interest rates of two banks

questions.question_text: The JAM trinity that supports the digital finance in India consists of:
options: Joint accounts, assets and mortgages
Justice, administration and money
Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and Mobile numbers
Jobs, agriculture and manufacturing

questions.question_text: The merchant discount rate (MDR) is:
options: A fee charged to the merchant on the digital payment accepted
A tax paid by the customer on the purchase
A discount given to the customer on the purchase
A subsidy paid to the bank by the government

questions.question_text: The zero MDR on UPI and RuPay debit cards was introduced to:
options: Promote digital payments by reducing the cost to merchants
Discourage the use of the cards by the customers
Increase the profits of the banks on the digital payments
Penalise the merchants who accept the cash

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of the NEFT service now?
options: It operates only for the first week of every month
It operates round the clock on all days, including holidays
It operates only up to noon on the working days
It operates only on the working days of the bank

questions.question_text: Settlement in NEFT is on a:
options: Deferred net basis, in batches
Monthly basis through a ledger
Daily basis through a cheque
Real-time gross basis, one by one

questions.question_text: Settlement in RTGS is on a:
options: Quarterly basis through a ledger
Real-time gross basis, one transaction at a time
Deferred net basis, in batches
Daily basis through a cheque

questions.question_text: The IFSC code, used for electronic fund transfers, has:
options: 11 characters, with the first four letters indicating the bank
16 digits, with the first six digits indicating the bank
9 digits, with the first four digits indicating the branch
12 characters, with the last four characters indicating the bank

questions.question_text: The IFSC code identifies a:
options: Particular type of account
Particular ATM
Particular bank branch
Particular customer

questions.question_text: Which of these is a valid format for a UPI ID?
options: ravi@oksbi
ravi#1234
ravi.sbi.com

questions.question_text: A person sends Rs 5,000 to a wrong UPI ID by mistake. The FIRST step should be to:
options: Wait for the receiver to return the money by himself
Send the same amount again to the correct person
Post the details on a social media platform for help
Raise a dispute with the app and the bank with the transaction details

questions.question_text: The reference number of a UPI transaction (UTR) helps the user to:
options: Track the payment and raise a complaint if required
Open a new account in another bank
Change the UPI PIN of the account
Increase the daily limit of the account

questions.question_text: Which of the following is likely to be a "static QR" feature?
options: The code changes for every transaction with a new amount
The code contains the password of the merchant
The code displays a fixed amount which cannot be changed
The code displays a fixed merchant ID and the customer enters the amount

questions.question_text: A dynamic QR code is generated:
options: Once for the customer to be shown in the app
Once for the shop and printed on the wall for ever
For each transaction with the amount and details included
Once for the bank and kept in the branch

questions.question_text: "Credit on UPI" allows a customer to:
options: Pay through a cheque that is attached to the UPI ID
Pay through a pre-approved credit line or a RuPay credit card linked to UPI
Pay through a loan that the app grants without a bank
Pay in cash at the shop and get a credit later

questions.question_text: Buy Now Pay Later schemes pose a risk to young users mainly because they:
options: Encourage spending beyond means and can lead to debt
Charge no interest or fees under any circumstances
Are banned by law for all the customers
Always reduce the credit score of the user

questions.question_text: Aadhaar-based e-KYC helps banks and wallet issuers to:
options: Verify the identity of a customer quickly without the paper documents
Give an unlimited loan to the customer without a credit check
Share the account details with other customers
Waive the charges on the accounts for the customer

questions.question_text: DigiLocker is a government platform for:
options: Storing the shares of the companies of the citizens
Storing and sharing the digital copies of official documents
Storing the passwords of the bank accounts
Storing the cash and the jewellery of the citizens

tests.title: Unit 3: Digital Payment Mechanism – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: The Account Aggregator framework allows a customer to:
options: Merge all the bank accounts into one account automatically
Share the financial data with the regulated entities by giving consent
Close all the dormant accounts without the knowledge
Borrow without any credit history

questions.question_text: The ONDC is intended to:
options: Merge the public sector banks into a large bank
Manage the pension funds of the employees
Create an open network on which buyers and sellers can transact across platforms
Replace the stock exchanges for the trading of shares

questions.question_text: The National Common Mobility Card is designed to:
options: Allow a single card to be used for the cash deposits only
Allow a single card to be used for the share trading
Allow a single card to be used for the cheque payments
Allow a single card to be used for transit and retail payments

questions.question_text: The daily UPI transaction limit for most person-to-person payments is:
options: There is no limit under any circumstance
Rs 1,000 for every user
Rs 1 lakh, with a higher limit for specified categories
Rs 10 crore for every user

questions.question_text: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act requires organisations to:
options: Sell the personal data to the advertisers for the revenue
Process personal data lawfully with the consent of the individual
Publish the personal data on the public websites
Delete all the personal data on a daily basis

questions.question_text: On losing a mobile phone that has banking apps, the user should:
options: Block the SIM, inform the bank and change the passwords at once
Wait for a month in the hope of finding the phone
Ignore the matter as the phone has a screen lock
Post the PIN on social media to warn the others

questions.question_text: A secure website address begins with:
options: https, which indicates an encrypted connection
www, which indicates a government connection
ftp, which indicates a file transfer connection
http, which indicates an encrypted connection

questions.question_text: The padlock symbol in the browser's address bar shows that:
options: The site is owned by the government and is free of fraud
The site is approved by the RBI and guaranteed safe
The site is free of malware and cannot steal data
The connection is encrypted, but the site may not be trustworthy

questions.question_text: A user logs in with a password, then confirms with a fingerprint and an OTP. This is:
options: Single-factor authentication
Biometric registration
Multi-factor authentication
Password recovery

questions.question_text: An attacker secretly intercepts the communication between a customer and the bank. This is a:
options: Denial of service attack
Man-in-the-middle attack
Skimming attack
Ransomware attack

questions.question_text: Software that locks the data of a user and demands a payment to unlock it is:
options: Adware
Spyware
Freeware
Ransomware

questions.question_text: Regular updating of the mobile banking app is important mainly because the updates:
options: Raise the limit of the daily transaction
Reduce the charges of the account
Fix the security vulnerabilities in the app
Increase the size of the screen of the phone

questions.question_text: Which of the following will a genuine bank NEVER ask a customer to disclose?
options: The PIN, OTP, CVV or net banking password
The branch name where the account is held
The type of the account held with the bank
The name of the account holder with the bank

questions.question_text: Digital payments help in formalising the economy because they:
options: Leave a record of transactions which helps the tax and regulatory work
Hide the source and destination of the money from the authorities
Increase the use of cash in the day-to-day transactions
Reduce the need for the banks in the system

questions.question_text: An online seller asks the buyer to pay into a personal UPI ID instead of the official payment page. This is a:
options: Standard practice for a genuine e-commerce site
Rule of the government for the online sales
Red flag for a possible fraud
Requirement of the RBI for small sellers

questions.question_text: A bank imposes a short delay before a large first-time transfer to a new payee. The purpose is to:
options: Raise the income of the bank from the fees
Reduce fraud by giving time to review the transaction
Test the speed of the network of the bank
Discourage the customers from using the digital mode

questions.question_text: A merchant uses a "soundbox" at the counter. Its main use is to:
options: Print the receipt for the customer
Announce the receipt of each payment by audio
Grant a loan to the merchant
Dispense the cash to the customers

questions.question_text: The safest way to download a bank's mobile app is from:
options: The official app store or the link on the bank's website
A stranger's phone through a file sharing app
A file forwarded in a messaging group
A link sent in an unknown SMS message

questions.question_text: Which behaviour BEST reduces the risk of phishing?
options: Replying to the e-mails with the personal details
Forwarding the suspicious message to all the contacts
Clicking on every link received in an e-mail
Checking the sender and avoiding clicks on suspicious links

questions.question_text: Cash on delivery differs from the digital payment in that the payment is:
options: Made in cash when the goods are delivered
Made through the wallet at the time of the order
Made by a post-dated cheque at the time of the order
Made online before the goods are dispatched

questions.question_text: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 gives the power to regulate payment systems to the:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Reserve Bank of India

questions.question_text: An NBFC-run digital lending app asks for access to the contacts, photos and location of the borrower's phone. Under the RBI norms, this is:
options: Allowed, if the borrower is a first-time borrower
Not permitted, as the apps must not access such data without need
Required, as the RBI wants the data for the credit report
Allowed, as the lender needs it to assess the creditworthiness

questions.question_text: The "cooling-off" or look-up period in digital lending allows a borrower to:
options: Postpone the payments for a year without any interest
Avoid the repayment if the borrower changes his mind later
Increase the loan amount without any additional documents
Exit the loan by paying the principal and the proportionate interest

questions.question_text: The key benefit of the interoperability in QR codes for the merchant is that the merchant:
options: Cannot accept payments from the customers of foreign banks
Needs a separate code for the customers of each app
Needs only one code to accept payments from the customers of any app
Needs to open a separate bank account for each app

questions.question_text: The charges that the customers pay for P2P UPI payments are generally:
options: Equal to the MDR charged to the merchant
Fixed at Rs 100 for every transaction
Fixed at 10% of the amount
Nil under the present policy

tests.title: Unit 3: Digital Payment Mechanism – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: A customer should always check which detail before approving a UPI payment on the screen?
options: The model of the phone being used
The colour of the app and the theme
The name of the payee displayed and the amount
The number of the contacts in the phone

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of "two-factor authentication" for the card-not-present transactions in India?
options: Only the card number and the expiry date
Only the name of the card holder
An additional factor like the OTP or the PIN apart from the card details
Only the CVV of the card

questions.question_text: A user receives an e-mail with an attachment from an unknown sender. The best action is to:
options: Forward it to the friends for their opinion
Delete it without opening the attachment or the link
Open the attachment to check the contents
Reply with the bank details to verify the sender

questions.question_text: The Bharat QR code is:
options: A QR code for the identification of the voter
A QR code accepted by a single bank only
A QR code that can be used for the cash deposit only
A common QR code accepted by many card networks and UPI

questions.question_text: After a loan app's recovery agent threatens a borrower, the borrower should:
options: Report to the lender's grievance cell and, if needed, to the RBI and the police
Ignore the threats and stop the repayment altogether
Share the contacts with the agent to settle the matter
Pay immediately whatever the agent demands

questions.question_text: The principle of "customer protection" in digital banking means that the bank must:
options: Pass on the entire risk of the fraud to the customers
Ensure safe transactions and provide a grievance redressal system
Stop sending the alerts of the transactions to the customers
Avoid informing the customers of the changes in the charges

questions.question_text: A person gets a message about winning a prize in a lottery and is asked to pay a fee through UPI to get the prize. This is most likely:
options: A promotion by the bank where the account is held
A legitimate scheme by the government
A fraud to get the money from the person
A refund of the excess tax paid

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be an example of "push" payment?
options: The payee requests the money from the payer
The government pays the subsidy
The bank debits the account for the fees
The payer initiates the payment to the payee's account

questions.question_text: A "collect" or "pull" payment is initiated by the:
options: Payer, who sends the money to the payee
Regulator, which collects the penalty
Payee, who requests the money from the payer
Bank, which debits the account of the customer

questions.question_text: A merchant wants to receive the settlement of digital payments directly into the current account. The merchant needs to:
options: Obtain a licence from the SEBI as a stock broker
Open a savings account in the name of a minor
Register as a merchant with an acquiring bank or a payment aggregator
Apply to the RBI for the licence as a bank

questions.question_text: A payment aggregator in digital payments:
options: Collects the taxes from the merchants
Collects payments for many merchants and settles the amounts to them
Issues the currency notes for the merchants
Audits the accounts of the merchants

questions.question_text: If a card is used abroad for an online purchase without being enabled for international use, the transaction will:
options: Be declined, since the international usage is disabled by default
Be approved automatically without any authentication
Be approved only on the weekends
Be approved only if the amount is below Rs 100

questions.question_text: Setting a transaction limit on the card through the bank's app helps to:
options: Avoid the annual fee on the card
Increase the credit limit of the card
Limit the loss in case the card details are misused
Reduce the rate of interest on the card

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a safe way to store your passwords?
options: In the notes app on the phone with the label "bank PIN"
On a sticky note on the laptop screen
In a reputed password manager or in your memory
In an e-mail to yourself with the subject "passwords"

questions.question_text: The UPI mandate allows a customer to:
options: Withdraw cash without the debit card from the ATMs
Increase the daily limit beyond the NPCI's limit
Block the UPI ID of the other persons
Authorise recurring payments such as subscriptions with the UPI PIN

questions.question_text: An "e-NACH" mandate for the loan EMI is useful because it:
options: Reduces the interest rate on the loan automatically
Makes the loan interest-free for the first year
Allows the customer to skip the EMI without a penalty
Debits the EMI automatically from the account on the due date

questions.question_text: The RBI Ombudsman Scheme for digital transactions can be approached when:
options: The customer wants a discount on the loan
The bank or the wallet issuer has not resolved the complaint in 30 days
The customer has not made the complaint to the bank at all
The customer wants a higher rate on the deposits

questions.question_text: The Reserve Bank "Digital Payments Intelligence Platform" and the fraud registries are aimed at:
options: Printing the currency notes for the digital use
Fixing the interest rates of the deposits
Collecting the taxes on the digital payments
Detecting and preventing the frauds in the digital payments

questions.question_text: A person pays Rs 1 lakh through UPI for a purchase and gets the goods of low quality. Which statement is TRUE?
options: The payment can be reversed by the customer at any time on his own
The payment mode does not remove the consumer's rights under the consumer law
The payment is not covered by the consumer law as it is digital
The payment is the same as a gift and cannot be disputed

questions.question_text: The concept of "financial inclusion" in digital payments means:
options: Giving the poor and the rural access to the formal financial services at an affordable cost
Giving the government access to the private bank accounts
Giving the rich access to the exclusive financial services
Giving the foreign banks access to the Indian market

questions.question_text: Which of the following BEST describes the safe use of an ATM?
options: Sharing the PIN with a person standing behind in the queue
Writing the PIN on the card for ease of use
Leaving the card in the slot while checking the balance
Covering the keypad while entering the PIN and not accepting help from strangers

questions.question_text: A person uses the same password for e-mail, net banking and shopping sites. The main risk is that:
options: The password will be too strong to remember
The sites will charge a fee for the same password
The bank will freeze the account for the same password
A leak at one site can expose all the other accounts

questions.question_text: A bank customer's account is credited with Rs 50,000 by mistake. The customer should:
options: Inform the bank and return the amount, since it is not his money
Keep the amount since the bank made the error
Transfer it to a friend's account for safety
Spend the amount quickly before the bank notices

questions.question_text: A person who uses digital payments often wants to keep track of the spending. The best method is to:
options: Delete the SMS alerts every day
Review the statements and the app history regularly
Avoid checking the balance for the months
Depend on the memory alone

questions.question_text: The most important rule to follow in digital payments is:
options: Share the OTP only with the people who call from the bank
Never share the PIN, OTP, CVV or password with anyone
Use the same PIN for all the cards and the apps
Note the PIN on the back of the card for convenience
